To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the aza-MBH reaction of isatin ketimines with methyl vinyl ketone has been established by employing chiral amines and phosphines as the catalysts, and that the reaction resulted in 3-substitued 3-amino oxindoles in good yield and with excellent enantiomeric excess.
the aza-MBH reaction of MVK with isatin-derived ketiminium ions has been achieved by using chiral phosphine and amino catalysts.
the chiral quaternay stereogenic centers can be efficiently assembled by using chiral phosphine catalysts in the asymmetric aza-Morit-Baylis-Hilman reaction of MVK with isatin-derived ketamine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new and highly stereoselective method for the synthesis of aza-MBH products, in which the quaternary carbon center has a chiral center.
the development of new synthetic methods for the construction of biomedically important heterocyclic scaffolds with chiral quatemary stereocenters.
a highly enantioselective aza-Morata-Baylis-Hilman (aza-MBHI reaction) for the synthesis of optically active 3-substitued-3-aminoxindoles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the aza-MBH reaction of isatin ketimines with Michael acceptors can be catalyzed by chiral amino and/or phosphino compounds, resulting in biologically important 3-subtituted-3- amino-2-oxinodoles in high yields and with excellent enantiomeric excesses.
the aza-MBH reaction is a powerful method for the synthesis of biologically important 3-substitute 3-aminooxindoles in a highly enantioselective manner.
the aza-MBH reaction is a highly effective and efficient approach for the construction of biomedically important compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reaction of isatin-based ketimines with Michael acceptor is a very efficient way to access chiral quaternaries.
the aza-MBH reaction is an efficient and convenient method for the preparation of chiral quaternay carbon centers with high efficiency and selectivity.
a wide range of chiral quaternay carbon centers could be constructed in a single step by the catalytic asymmetric aza-Moritabaylis-Hillmann reaction of isatin ketimines with methyl vinyl ketone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reaction is highly dependent on both the nature of the catalyst and the substituents at the 5 and 6 positions of the isatin-derived ketamine, as well as the nature of the nucleophile.
the aza-MBH reaction of isatin ketimines is a powerful tool for the synthesis of chiral biologically important 3-subtituted 3-aminoisatin products.
the aza-MBH reaction can be performed with a broad range of ketimines and Michael acceptors.
